name: PCD8544
full_name: Philips/NXP PCD8544 48x84 Pixel Matrix LCD Controller/Driver
description: The PCD8544 is a low-power controller for the 48x84 pixel monochrome LCD made famous by the Nokia 3310/5110 phones, now sold as a cheap 8-pin graphic display module. It uses a 3.3V SPI-style serial interface (DIN, CLK) plus a DC line that selects command versus data and active-low chip-select and reset lines. A separate LIGHT pin controls the backlight LEDs. Its tiny size, ultra-low power draw, and on-chip 504-byte display RAM make it a long-time favorite for battery-powered gadgets and retro displays.

pins.name: RST
pins.description: active-low reset; must be pulsed low at power-up

pins.name: DC
pins.description: data/command select: high = data, low = command

pins.name: LIGHT
pins.description: backlight control (BL); LED backlight, often active-low on red modules

extra.addressing: horizontal or vertical banks of 8 pixels

typical_application: An 84x48 graphics/text display for battery-powered projects, driven over SPI (DIN, CLK, DC, SCE, RST) at 3.3V with the LIGHT pin switching the backlight, using the Adafruit_PCD8544 or u8g2 libraries.
gotchas: it is a 3.3V part: driving VCC or the logic lines at 5V can damage it; 5V MCUs need level shifting on all signal lines
RST must be pulsed low after power-up or the display stays blank or shows garbage
pin header order and labels vary between module batches (some swap RST/CE, some label BL/LED differently) - check the silkscreen
the LIGHT/backlight pin is active-low on many red modules (tie to GND to turn on) but active-high on others
the module is write-only; do not expect to read display RAM or status back
set a sensible contrast/bias (V_OP) in software or the image is invisible or all-black despite correct wiring
